messages.body_plain:
Hi Mamadou,

I tested with your data on two different machines now (mac and linux) and on both machines it worked fine with the files you uploaded.

Furthermore the error "File '/tmp/RtmpIDEBx8/Sample7_CHG.' has size 0. Returning a NULL data.frame." indicates that the uncompressed file is empty,
Are you sure that the files you are processing are not empty?

When I was testing your command multiple times I saw that the timestamps of the uncompressed files in my temp folder did not change,
so it is possible that, when running the uncompression multiple times the files are not overwritten.
If this is the case, and the uncompression failed the first time, the files won't be updated.
You could try to remove the files from the temp folder and retry.

Another possibilty is that the uncompression is silently failing and thereby the output will always be empty.

To mitigate the compression issues, you could uncompress yourself and use the uncompressed files as input for methRead.

Please let me know wether this works.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Inquiry about methylKit's regional Analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm so happy I'm finally able to post to this group!

I have a quick question regarding regional analysis using methylKit, specifically promoter analysis.

I did the following:
 I read the methylation call files to a methylRawList object: myobj
Then I read the gene BED file: gene.obj=readTranscriptFeatures("hg19_refseq_bed.txt")
Then I summarized methylation information over the promoters: promoters=regionCounts(myobj,gene.obj$promoters)
Then I filtered the promoters based on coverage: filtered.myobj = filterByCoverage(promoters,lo.count=5,lo.perc=NULL,hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)
Then I merged the samples using the unite function: meth=unite(filtered.myobj, destrand=TRUE)
Is this correct?
Did I have to filter for base coverage before summarizing methylation information over the promoters? Should I filter by base first then by promoters (filter two times)?
i.e. do the following
Read the methylation call files to a methylRawList object: myobj
Filtering samples based on base read coverage: filtered.myobj=filterByCoverage(myobj,lo.count=10,lo.perc=NULL,hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)
Read the gene BED file: gene.obj=readTranscriptFeatures("hg19_refseq_bed.txt")
Summarize methylation information over the promoters: promoters=regionCounts( filtered.myobj ,gene.obj$promoters)
Filter promoters again based on coverage: filtered.myobj2 = filterByCoverage(promoters,lo.count=5,lo.perc=NULL,hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)
Merge the samples using the unite function: meth=unite(filtered.myobj2, destrand=TRUE)

All the best,
Sarah

T

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Inquiry about methylKit::normalize.Coverage()
messages.body_plain:
I think it is not necessary to do normalization if the coverage values are systematically different for samples, this has to be tested maybe with simulation data for now let's assume it is not. filtering works for RRBS mostly when you have high read counts and it is not a good idea to remove PCR duplicates with RRBS due to the nature of the protocol. There is no guideline but it might be a good idea to remove the 95 or 99th percentile if you can't remove the PCR duplicates.

Best,
altuna

messages.subject: Analysis without treatment
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I want to obtain genome-wide methylation profiles for all three contexts, later I will annotate with various genomic features. But first, I want to make sure that regions are significantly methylated in each genome of my samples(as coverage per se is not enough to tell that). I don't know how to conduct "DMR without treatment". I have come up with a plan, l want to hear your comment. It is not a good solution I am aware, and hope there is a better way to cope with my issue.

Plan:

I have 1 organism and 3 bismark cytosine report outputs, each for different contexts. I generated three objects to see methylation profiles and coverage. However, before annotation I want to get significance level of methylated sites. DMR analysis need two groups, so I thought I can generate objects with binary combinations of three contexts given as test and control. Like this:

myobjDB_CG_CHG = methRead(location = "CysRep1.CG_report.txt", "CysRep1.CHG_report.txt"
                      sample.id <http://sample.id> = "Rep1", assembly = "mtr4",
                      treatment = c(0,1),
                      pipeline = "bismarkCytosineReport",
                      dbtype = "tabix", mincov = 10)

Thanks in advance,

Asuman
